label: Sidak-Khatri
title: Remark
body_md:
Suppose $H_0^{(n)}$ holds, i.e., $\mu = 0$. Note that  \cite{sidak1967rectangular} and \cite{khatri1967certain}  proved that  for any $a_1, \ldots, a_n\geq 0$, 
\begin{align}\label{Sidak-Khatri}
\mathbb P \big( |X_1|\leq a_1, \ldots, |X_n|\leq a_n\big) \geq \prod_{i=1}^n \mathbb P (|X_i|\leq a_i)\,. 
\end{align}
If we let $R$ be the hypercube 
\begin{equation} \label{DefineR} 
R = \cap_{i = 1}^n R_i,
\end{equation} 
where $R_i = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n: |x_i| \leq a_i\}$ is the $i$-th coordinate slab 
 bounded by  two hyperplanes $\{x = (x_1, \ldots, x_n):  x_i =a_i\}$ and 
 $\{x = (x_1, \ldots, x_n): x_i = -a_i\}$, 
their result can be restated as that the probability that $X$ lies in the hypercube is at least the product 
of the probabilities that $X$ lies in each of the $n$ slabs. 
  In comparison, the GCI applies to much broader settings, where if the event is the intersection of $K$ ($K$ can be any integer)  
  centrally symmetric and convex sets: 
\[
G = \cap_{k = 1}^K G_k, 
\] 
then 
\[
\mathbb{P}(X \in G) \geq \Pi_{i = 1}^K \mathbb{P}(X \in G_k). 
\] 
For the three testing problems we consider above, we can use (\ref{Sidak-Khatri}) to address the first one. 
However, for more general settings such as the hybrid test, (\ref{Sidak-Khatri}) does not apply, 
and we must use Royen's GCI.

label: thm:two-sided
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:two-sided} 
For any correlation matrix $\Sigma$ and any  $x$, $F_n(x; \Sigma) \geq F_n(x; I_n)$.  
Moreover, fix $0 < \alpha < 1$ and consider the max-type test (\ref{MTT}) with $t = t_n$ in (\ref{Definetn}). 
For any correlation matrix $\Sigma$, the Type I error is no more than $\alpha$. Also,  when $\Sigma = I_n$, the Type I error is exactly $\alpha$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Let $R$ be the hypercube defined in (\ref{DefineR})  with $a_1 = a_2= \ldots =a_n = x$.   Then we have 
\[
F(x, \Sigma) = \mathbb{P}(Z \in R).   
\] 
In this special case,  Royen's GCI reduces to (\ref{Sidak-Khatri}), so  we can also prove Theorem \ref{thm:two-sided} using the \v{S}id\'ak--Khatri inequality.  But as mentioned in Remark 1,  in more complicated  settings,  
(\ref{Sidak-Khatri}) may not apply, and we must use Royen's GCI.

label: thm:hybrid
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:hybrid} 
Consider the hybrid test $H_n$ where we reject the null when $T_n > t_1$ or $S_n > t_2$ or $Q_n > t_3$ with $t_1, t_2, t_3$ given in (\ref{hybrid-threshold}).   
Then the Type I error of the test is no more than
\[
1 - (1 - \alpha) \mathbb{P}(S_n \leq \sqrt{a_n} x_0) \mathbb{P}(Q_n \leq \sqrt{b_n} y_0) = 1 - (1 -\alpha) \mathbb{P}(|z| \leq x_0) \mathbb{P}(z \leq y_0) +o(1), 
\] 
which is valid for all $\Sigma$ such that ${\bf 1}_n' \Sigma {\bf 1}_n\neq 0$.

label: conj2
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj2} 
For any $n \times n$ correlation matrix $\Sigma$, $F_n^*(x; \Sigma) \geq F_n^*(x; \Sigma^*)$.

label: thm:Slepian
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: thm:FWER
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:FWER} 
Fix $0 < \alpha < 1$ and consider the HT test for (\ref{null1}) with $t_n$ in (\ref{HT2}).    
For any correlation matrix $\Sigma$, the FWER is no more than $\alpha$.  
In the special case of $\Sigma = I_n$, the FWER is $1 - (1 - \alpha)^{n_0 /n}$, which is 
nearly $\alpha$ when $n_0 / n \approx 1$.
head: environment

title: Proofs
body_md: Theorems~\ref{thm:two-sided}, \ref{thm:hybrid}, and \ref{thm:FWER} are immediate consequences of GCI, since the events involved are all symmetric and convex. Moreover, Conjecture~\ref{conj2} directly implies Theorem~\ref{thm:Slepian}. Therefore, we omit the proofs.
